claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic HEA has dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The internal boundaries in the initial alloy are inherently weak.
Weak internal boundaries predispose the initial alloy to microcracking and brittle behavior during room-temperature tensile loading.
Adding approximately 0.2–0.5 wt% B and homogenizing at 1100–1150 °C for 1–2 hours will cause selective B segregation at internal lamellar-colony boundaries.
B enrichment at the internal boundaries will reduce interfacial energy.
B enrichment will improve bonding and cohesive strength between the phases at internal boundaries.
B acts as a boundary-active element in the proposed alloy.
Homogenization enables B to segregate to interphase boundaries.
Lower boundary energy and enhanced interfacial cohesion will delay microcrack nucleation under tensile stress.
Lower boundary energy and enhanced interfacial cohesion will impede microcrack propagation under tensile stress.
A refined interfacial structure produced by B addition will contribute to increased alloy strength.
The B-modified alloy will have greater tensile strength than the undoped baseline.
The B-modified alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the undoped baseline.
Atom probe tomography and TEM will reveal localized B enrichment at colony boundaries.
B modification will delay microcrack initiation relative to the undoped baseline.
B modification will shift fracture behavior from brittle toward more ductile failure modes.
The expected benefits require the B concentration to remain within approximately 0.2–0.5 wt% and the homogenization treatment to promote segregation without brittle boride precipitation.
Excess B or inappropriate thermal processing may cause excessive boride precipitation or embrittlement.
